title: Republicans block impeachment push against Pete Hegseth
summary: Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives voted Tuesday to sideline a resolution that aimed to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.

blocks.text: Hegseth calls effort to impeach him 'a political spectacle'
Republicans in the U.S. House of Representatives voted Tuesday evening to sideline a resolution that aimed to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.
The vote halts the effort spearheaded by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie to remove the Pentagon chief for his conduct in office and his handling of the war in Iran.
More to come
Massie, who won't be in Congress when the new session begins in January, filed a privileged motion on the House floor on Monday to introduce eight articles of impeachment.

Impeachment resolutions can carry over to the next session, which begins on Jan. 3 with Democrats holding the House and Senate majority. If the House were to impeach and a Senate trial were to occur, the threshold for a conviction and removal from office requires two-thirds of senators voting in favour.

Hegseth said any such proceedings would be a "show trial against the president and the secretary of war" and he characterized the articles of impeachment as "policy disagreements" that don't meet the impeachment standard of high crimes and misdemeanours.
"The proper remedy for a policy disagreement, it's legislation, it's debate, it's the next presidential election," said Hegseth, holding his first press briefing from the Pentagon since May.
U.S. House Republican moves to force vote on impeaching Pete Hegseth
U.S. President Donald Trump gave an enthusiastic response on social media to Hegseth's pushback. Trump has said he would stand by Hegseth even if he is impeached.

Under the rules of Massie's motion, a vote is supposed to be held within two legislative days unless a majority supports a countering motion to kill the effort. Massie introduced a similar measure in September, but the House legislators were sent home before a vote could occur.
A vote in the House could come by mid-week, but the next steps are highly uncertain.
'They will fail again'

The articles of impeachment in Massie's motion lead with the lack of congressional authorization for the war in Iran. The articles also reference Hegseth's role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela, and the deadly strikes on boats allegedly transporting drugs in waters near South America.
"I stand behind every one of these operations," Hegseth said on Tuesday.

He said "thousands of American lives" were saved with every boat strike — even as human rights organizations and international bodies have said they possibly constitute crimes against humanity. Hegseth also said that former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro was "not kidnapped, he was brought to justice by America's best."
Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky speaks Monday outside the Capitol about articles of impeachment against Hegseth. (Allison Robbert/The Associated Press)
The articles also refer to attempts to prosecute Congress members Mark Kelly and Elissa Slotkin after they recorded a video advising service members they were not obliged to follow illegal orders.

Massie, who was defeated earlier this year by a Trump-backed Republican opponent in a primary, pushed forward an impeachment resolution over the objections of House Republican leadership, with outgoing Speaker Mike Johnson saying it would be "a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see."

blocks.text: The last House impeachment was of former Homeland Security chief Alejandro Mayorkas in Joe Biden's administration in 2024, for breach of public trust and willful refusal to comply with the law. The Republican-led House cited the surge of migrants at the southern border in just the second ever impeachment of a cabinet secretary, but the Democratic-led Senate then never took up the measure.

Trump was twice impeached in the House, in 2019 and 2021, but acquitted at Senate trials. In the second impeachment, many Republicans argued that Trump's actions leading up to the 2021 Capitol riot were best dealt with in the courts, but Trump completed a remarkable political comeback before criminal indictments he faced were resolved legally.
Hegseth called those Trump impeachments failures and predicted that the current efforts "will fail again."
Razor-thin confirmation
What constitutes "high crimes and misdemeanours" is not spelled out in the Constitution, leaving it to lawmakers to decide.

Democrat Hakeem Jeffries, Johnson's potential successor as the next Speaker, recently said he is a"hard yes" for impeaching Hegseth. Several other Democrats took to social media on Tuesday to say they were in favour.
A vote will put pressure on Republicans, many of whom blamed their midterm election wipeout on the Iran war.
Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska, who has been critical of Hegseth, told reporters on Tuesday he wasn't a fan of the impeachment articles in their present form. (Jacquelyn Martin/The Associated Press)
Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska has highlighted other concerns not contained in the articles, including Hegseth's firing of dozens of senior military leaders, but he also questioned Massie's motives.
"If we were allowed to amend it, I'd maybe feel a lot of differently," said Bacon.
Republican Rep. Warren Davidson of Ohio said, "blaming Hegseth for a duty Congress shirked and the president made is wrong."
"This isn't about Iran, this about the fact that Pete took on the bureaucracy at the Pentagon," said Vice-President JD Vance.

Vance broke a tie in the Senate to enable Hegseth's confirmation in early 2025. Republicans Susan Collins and Mitch McConnell — each set to leave Congress — voted against his confirmation, as did Republican Lisa Murkowski and all of the Senate Democrats.

Thom Tillis, a Republican also leaving the Senate, has expressed regret for his vote to confirm Hegseth, saying in part in September that the secretary "retreats to ginning up culture wars instead of soberly attending to the vital work of our national defence."

Democrats and a handful of Republicans questioned Hegseth's fitness for the job nearly two years ago. Hegseth admitted paying a settlement to a woman who alleged he sexually assaulted her, in order to prevent a costly and drawn-out process.
His confirmation hearings also included allegations of excessive drinking and financial mismanagement at two veterans' organizations he previously led.

During Trump's first term, Hegseth was an on-air Fox News contributor who lobbied the president on behalf of three service members who faced accusations of war crimes in military tribunals, arguing they were being treated unfairly.

blocks.text: Trump ultimately granted clemency to two of the men, and elevated a third in rank.

Hegseth's tenure at the Pentagon has been unconventional, and that was on display on Tuesday. Defence secretaries typically stay away from partisan political statements, but Hegseth laid out criticisms of predecessor Lloyd Austin and disparaged the military recruitment and retention efforts of Biden's administration.
He also told the U.S. troops to "stay the course" while evoking his Christianity, even as he has been sued for imposing his religion on federal workers.
